title: His music collection and the Robichaux music
summary: Howard describes the music he kept from his big band days and the music Anna Robichaux gave him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I understand you have quite a collection of music, is that true? I'm not trying to put you on the spot and ask you everything that you know, but I just wondered, I mean I know that you're a musician that knows more tunes than almost anybody around, I understand.

I have up in the front there, a whole lot of music when I had the big band. Willie Pajor and Bill Matthews, the way, with me and the big band. And I have a lot of music. A lot of music. And when Professor John Robichaud died, his wife was Anna, she gave me quite a bit of music. You know what I mean? At that time.
I've had a couple of books of John Robichaud's too with his name stamped on that I got from Maurice Durand or something like that.
That's right. Well, she gave, in other words she gave me half of a gift for Maurice because that was his supplement.
He still has some of them, but I'm in California.

Yeah, I'm in California. That's right. Well, yeah, most of us, when they want something, they come here to me. They go up there and get what they want, bring it back. They got music in there. I'm quite sure I couldn't play a note of it. I've been playing no music for so long. But I used to play. I used to play.
You've got a wonderful memory I know, among other things, the telephone numbers.
If I put my mind on it. You'd probably remember all those too if you'd, all the old numbers too from way back, if you had to play them, wouldn't you?
Well, my property would come to me if I had to play them, you know what I mean? But offhand now, man, you kind of got me.
